questions.question: Mitral annular calcification (MAC) is most easily identified on which modality?
questions.detail: CT is exquisitely sensitive to calcium; MAC appears as a dense, C-shaped calcification at the base of the mitral valve.

questions.question: In patients with infective endocarditis, CT is better than Echocardiography for identifying:
questions.detail: Cardiac CT provides excellent anatomical detail of the perivalvular tissues and extra-cardiac complications like septic emboli.

questions.question: Which valvular lesion is most strongly associated with 'annuloaortic ectasia' and Marfan syndrome?
questions.detail: Dilation of the aortic root in Marfan syndrome leads to aortic valve insufficiency (regurgitation).

questions.question: CMR quantification of 'Regurgitant Fraction' (RF) > 50% generally indicates:
questions.detail: An RF > 50% is a common threshold for severe valvular insufficiency on CMR.

questions.question: 'Paravalvular leak' is a complication of:
questions.detail: This occurs when blood flows around the outside of a prosthetic valve ring due to poor seating or infection.
